Required privacy clauses are banded by engagement type, with a named approver and a recorded route for an agreed departure.
Each party's record names the privacy obligations it is bound to and cites the agreement version carrying them.
The processing a party performs today falls within the terms of the agreement in force for it.
Each gap between signed terms and actual processing carries an owner and a date.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved schedule of required clauses banded by engagement type, with the approver named.
Obtain the recorded privacy obligations held for each party, with the agreement version cited.
Collect the coverage sweep naming every party checked and the agreement version relied on.
Request the executed agreements for a sample of parties drawn across the engagement bands.

Analysis:
Compare each sampled agreement with the clause schedule for its band and list every clause missing or weakened in negotiation.
Check that each departure from the schedule followed the recorded route and carries the approver's decision.
Set the recorded obligations against the party's current processing description and identify terms that no longer reach what is done.
Confirm every gap raised by the sweep has an owner and a date rather than being carried forward unassigned.

Output:
Clause conformance matrix for the sampled agreements against their band's schedule.
List of parties whose processing has moved beyond the terms in force.
Gap log extract showing the owner and date recorded for each open item.

title.en: Set out the privacy terms each class of engagement must carry

description.en: Work out, from the privacy objectives the organisation has set, which measures have to be binding rather than merely requested — return or deletion at exit, limits on onward disclosure and sub-processors, breach notification timing, where processing may happen, a right to evidence — and state which class of engagement each one applies to. Say who may approve a departure and how it is recorded, because pressure to drop a clause arrives at signature rather than at drafting. Cover the case where the organisation signs the counterparty's standard terms and cannot edit them: name which measures an addendum has to carry instead, and which absences make the engagement unacceptable.

evidenceHint.en: Approved schedule of required clauses banded by engagement type, naming the approver and the route for an agreed departure.

title.en: Record the privacy obligations each party is bound to

description.en: Per party, capture the obligations that have actually been agreed with them and where those obligations are written down, including any shared or multi-party arrangement the organisation has joined that carries obligations of its own. Where an assessment identified a needed obligation that was not agreed, record that gap against the party.

title.en: Match the signed terms against the processing each party performs today

description.en: Take each party in the ecosystem ranking, pull the agreement actually in force — base contract plus every amendment, order form and renewal that varies it — and compare the privacy measures it binds the party to with what that party now does with data. Long-standing suppliers commonly run on paper signed before the current clause set existed, and an auto-renewal moves the end date without touching a single term. List every party whose terms are absent, lapsed, or narrower than its processing, and name who will renegotiate, cut back what the party receives, or accept the position.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage sweep naming every party checked, the agreement version relied on, and each gap raised with an owner and a date.

templates.title: Interoperability and multi-party approaches
templates.description: Implements ID.DE-P4: Interoperability frameworks or similar multi-party approaches are used to manage data processing ecosystem privacy risks.
templates.objective: To ensure data shared among several organisations moves under one common set of privacy provisions that each connected system implements, rather than under bilateral assumption.
templates.successCriteria:
Each shared processing arrangement names the instrument it runs under, or is recorded as an accepted exception.
Every covered exchange has a conformance profile answering, provision by provision, how it is implemented.
Divergences from the framework are listed and approved in advance rather than discovered during an exchange.
Each arrangement is reviewed against the framework version now in force, not the version adopted at the outset.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the schedule of multi-party arrangements with the chosen instrument and the accepted exceptions recorded.
Obtain the conformance profile for each covered exchange, provision by provision.
Collect the accepted divergence list and the approver named on it.
Obtain the dated comparison notes recording the framework version reviewed for each arrangement.

Analysis:
Check the schedule against the systems that actually exchange data with other organisations and identify arrangements running under no instrument.
Test a sample of profile entries against the configuration of the exchanging system rather than against the profile's own assertion.
Compare the divergences visible in the profiles with the accepted divergence list and flag those never approved.
Set the version cited in each comparison note against the framework version now published and list arrangements reviewed against a superseded one.

Output:
Arrangement coverage table showing the instrument or accepted exception for each.
Profile verification results for the sampled provisions, naming the system evidence relied on.
List of unapproved divergences and of arrangements reviewed against a superseded version.

title.en: Decide which shared processing arrangements will run under a multi-party framework

description.en: Where three or more parties handle the same data, pairwise agreements leave the seams unowned: every pair is covered and the end-to-end outcome is nobody's. List the arrangements of that shape and name, for each, the framework, code of conduct, certification scheme or consortium rulebook it will run under. Where no suitable instrument exists, say so, name what carries the exposure instead, and who accepted that position.

evidenceHint.en: Schedule of multi-party arrangements with the chosen instrument beside each, and the accepted exceptions named.

title.en: Implement the interoperability framework's privacy provisions in each system exchanging data under it

description.en: Joining a framework changes nothing until the systems actually emit and honour what it specifies — purpose codes, consent or preference signals, retention markers, and the agreed way parties refer to the same individual. Work through every exchange the framework covers and set down, provision by provision, what is implemented, what a local equivalent stands in for, and what the organisation does not do at all. An unimplemented provision is a divergence to carry openly, with the person who accepted it, rather than an intention.

evidenceHint.en: Conformance profile per covered exchange, provision by provision, with the accepted divergence list and its approver.

title.en: Re-examine each multi-party arrangement against the framework version now in force

description.en: Frameworks are revised, participants join and leave, and a profile that conformed at signature quietly stops conforming without anyone being told. For each arrangement, compare what the organisation operates today against the published version currently in force, and check whether the parties named at the outset are still the parties involved. Record a decision for every divergence found — adopt the change, seek an exception, or withdraw from the arrangement — with the date it takes effect.

evidenceHint.en: Dated comparison note per arrangement listing the version reviewed, divergences found and the decision recorded for each.

templates.title: Routine assessment of ecosystem parties
templates.description: Implements ID.DE-P5: Ecosystem parties are routinely assessed using audits, test results, or other evaluations to confirm they are meeting their contractual, interoperability-framework, and other obligations.
templates.objective: To ensure what a party promised is confirmed by evidence produced outside the organisation's own confidence in it, at an interval matched to the exposure that party carries.
templates.successCriteria:
The acceptable evaluation forms, the interval owed per exposure tier, and the consequence of supplying none are issued as a standard.
Each high-priority party's file holds an independent evaluation with its date and source recorded.
An assessor's note states which recorded obligations each evaluation addressed and which it did not.
A party without a current evaluation has a decision recorded against it, naming the decision-maker and the date.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the issued standard naming acceptable evaluation forms, the interval per exposure tier and the stated consequence.
Obtain the per-party files holding the evaluations received, with their dates and sources.
Collect the assessor notes mapping each evaluation onto the obligations recorded for that party.
Obtain the decision list covering parties whose evaluation is missing or out of date.

Analysis:
Set the date of each evaluation held against the interval its tier owes and count the parties running past it.
Read the assessor notes for parties holding obligations no evaluation addressed, and judge whether reliance was placed on them regardless.
Test whether the stated consequence was actually applied to parties that supplied nothing, or whether the relationship simply continued.
Check that a decision to accept a missing evaluation was taken by someone other than the relationship's own manager.

Output:
Currency table of evaluations held against the interval owed by each tier.
Obligation coverage summary showing which recorded obligations no evaluation reaches.
List of parties continuing without a current evaluation and the decision recorded for each.

title.en: Fix what counts as an acceptable evaluation, and how often each tier owes one

description.en: Routine re-assessment collapses without a stated bar: one party sends a current audit report, another a two-year-old certificate, a third a completed questionnaire it filled in itself, and all three are filed as evidence. Say which forms are acceptable — independent audit, penetration test result, certification against a named scheme, a supervised control test — and set the interval each exposure tier owes, so a lapsed evaluation is a date arithmetic rather than a judgement call. Name what happens when a party supplies nothing, because an interval with no consequence behind it is a reminder, not a control.

evidenceHint.en: The standard as issued: acceptable evaluation forms, the interval per exposure tier, and the stated consequence for a party that supplies none.

title.en: Obtain an independent evaluation for each high-priority party

description.en: Ask each high-priority party for whatever evidence of its conduct exists — an audit result, a test result, a certification, or another party's evaluation — and record what it showed measured against the obligations recorded for that party. Record refusals and non-responses as outcomes rather than leaving the entry blank.

evidenceHint.en: Per-party file holding the evaluation received, its date and source, and the assessor's note of which recorded obligations it did and did not address.

title.en: Decide the standing of each party whose evaluation is missing or stale

description.en: List the parties with no current evaluation and, for each, record the decision taken — chase, restrict what they receive, accept the gap, or end the engagement — with the person who took it. A party left undecided is the outcome this task exists to prevent.

evidenceHint.en: Decision list naming each party without a current evaluation, the decision taken, the decision-maker and the date.

templates.title: Privacy values and the conditions they set
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P1: Organizational privacy values and policies (e.g., conditions on data processing such as data uses or retention periods, individuals' prerogatives with respect to data processing) are established and communicated.
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation's stated privacy position is expressed concretely enough to settle whether a particular use of data, or a particular period of holding it, is permitted.
templates.successCriteria:
The privacy values are recorded with the conditions they place on processing, in terms that decide a case rather than state an intention.
Each data category held carries a deletion point and a statement of the uses allowed and refused.
A category with no condition set has a named owner rather than a blank entry.
Data actions are checked against the condition set and those governed by no condition are listed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the recorded privacy values and the conditions they place on processing.
Obtain the condition table listing each data category, its deletion point, and the uses allowed and refused.
Collect the coverage list naming each data action checked and the condition found over it.
Request the owner recorded against each category still without a condition.

Analysis:
Put two live processing questions to the stated conditions and test whether they decide the questions without further interpretation.
Compare the categories appearing in the condition table with the data categories the inventory shows are actually held.
Sample stored data against the deletion point set for its category and identify holdings kept beyond it.
Confirm the data actions listed as ungoverned were raised for a condition rather than recorded and left standing.

Output:
Decision test note recording the questions put and the conditions that answered them.
Category comparison between the condition table and the data inventory.
List of data actions under no condition, with the owner assigned to each.

title.en: Write down the organisation's privacy values and the conditions they place on processing

description.en: State the values the organisation holds about data, then translate each into concrete conditions that bind processing — what data may be used for, how long it may be held, and what an individual may ask of it. Values with no condition beneath them are a preamble, so pair each one with at least a condition someone could breach.

title.en: Set the retention period and permitted uses for each category of data held

description.en: A value binds nothing until it names data and a number, so take the categories from the processing inventory and write against each the period after which the data goes, the uses it may be put to, and the uses ruled out. Where two conditions land on the same category and disagree, an analysis wanting three years of history against a twelve-month deletion, decide which one governs now rather than leaving both on the page for whoever operates the system to choose between. A category left without a stated period is not neutral: in practice it defaults to keeping the data forever, so leave those rows visible with an owner named against them.

evidenceHint.en: Condition table listing each data category, the deletion point set for it, the uses allowed and refused, and the owner of any category still blank.

title.en: Find the processing that no stated condition governs

description.en: Coverage fails quietly: every condition on the page is about processing somebody remembered, so the set looks complete when read from the inside. Work from the data actions inventory instead, taking each recorded action, finding the condition that governs what it may be used for and how long its data is kept, and listing the actions where nothing does. This does not ask whether practice obeyed the conditions; it asks which processing has nothing to obey, because an action with no condition over it is settled in practice by whoever operates it.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage list naming each data action checked, the condition found over it, and the actions left with none.

templates.title: Instilling privacy values in development
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P2: Processes to instill organizational privacy values within system/product/service development and operations are established and in place.
templates.objective: To ensure a privacy condition changes what is actually built and run, by travelling to delivery teams along a route that has been shown to stop a change the condition forbids.
templates.successCriteria:
Each privacy condition has a recorded means of reaching development and operations, naming a mechanism rather than an intention.
An exception carries the required fields, authorisation at the stated level, and a date by which it must be re-decided.
A change a privacy condition forbids is rejected at a stage that can be named.
Where a test case reached delivery unchallenged, the route was amended and the amendment recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the issued exception standard naming the required fields, the authorising level, and the maximum period an exception may run.
Obtain the record mapping each privacy condition to the mechanism carrying it into development and operations.
Collect the dated account of the forbidden change put through the delivery path and the stage that rejected it.
Retrieve the exceptions currently open, with their authorisation and re-decision dates.

Analysis:
Inspect the named mechanisms themselves, such as pipeline checks, review templates and backlog gates, and confirm each exists rather than being described.
Read the test account and establish whether rejection came from the mechanism claimed or from an individual happening to notice.
Check open exceptions against the standard's required fields and identify those past the date they should have been re-decided.
Confirm a route that failed to stop the test case was amended, and that the amendment was itself put to a fresh case.

Output:
Condition-to-mechanism map carrying the verification result for each mechanism.
Test case record showing the path travelled and the stage that intervened.
Exception register extract listing incomplete or expired authorisations.

title.en: State what an exception must record before work proceeds against a privacy value

description.en: Every delivery process grants exceptions, and the ones granted verbally are indistinguishable afterwards from a value nobody applied. Fix what an exception has to capture — which condition is being set aside, for which piece of work, who authorised it, what compensates, and when it lapses — and put a ceiling on how long one may run unreviewed. Without a lapse date an exception becomes the new default, and the value survives only in the document nobody reads.

evidenceHint.en: The exception standard as issued, naming the fields an exception must carry, the authorising level, and the maximum period one may run before it is re-decided.

title.en: Record the means by which each privacy condition reaches development and operations

description.en: Take each condition written down beside the organisation's privacy values and record what carries it into the work of building and running systems — a standard or template it is written into, a default the platform already enforces, a question the change record asks, an approval that cannot be given without it — and for each name where a person doing that work meets it and who is accountable for keeping it there. A condition with nothing carrying it stays as a visible row with its owner named against it. This task records the carrier inside the work; instruction on what the conditions mean is delivered under the awareness control, and the data decision required at each life-cycle stage is recorded separately.

title.en: Test the delivery path with a change a privacy condition forbids

description.en: A route that has never refused anything looks identical to one nobody consults. Send a deliberate case through the normal path — a design, a ticket or a configuration change that plainly breaches one of the recorded conditions — and note which stage catches it, or that it reached release untouched. Run it on the real path with the usual reviewers rather than asking whether the step exists; what matters is where the work stopped, not that the step is written down.

evidenceHint.en: Dated account of the case put through, the route it travelled, the stage that rejected it or the point it reached unchallenged, and the change made to the path afterwards.

templates.title: Workforce privacy roles and responsibilities
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P3: Roles and responsibilities for the workforce are established with respect to privacy.
templates.objective: To ensure every privacy duty the organisation relies on rests with a role a named person holds today, and that the workforce has been given the policies stating those duties.
templates.successCriteria:
Each role's privacy responsibilities are recorded together with the point at which they end.
The distribution record shows the policy version issued, the population it went to, and the date each part received it.
Every recorded privacy duty maps to a role a named person currently holds.
A duty found unowned is placed with a role rather than noted and carried into the next review.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the role records setting out privacy responsibilities and the limits stated for each.
Obtain the distribution record showing the policy version issued, the recipient population and the issue dates.
Collect the per-responsibility check naming the role each duty sits with and the person holding that role.
Request the placement decision for each duty previously found unowned.

Analysis:
Compare the recipient population in the distribution record with the current workforce list, including joiners arriving after the issue date.
Trace a sample of duties from the role map to the person holding the role and identify roles standing vacant.
Look for duties that two roles each record as ending at the other's boundary, leaving the work between them held by neither.
Check that duties previously found unowned now sit against a role rather than reappearing unchanged.

Output:
Distribution coverage comparison between the issued population and the current workforce.
Duty-to-holder trace showing vacant roles and boundary gaps.
List of duties placed since the last review, naming the role each went to.

title.en: Record the privacy responsibilities of each role and where they end

description.en: For every workforce role that touches data, state what it is responsible for doing and deciding, and state which of the adjacent responsibilities sit with an external party rather than with the role. Attach the resulting responsibility record, and name the role that resolves a boundary neither side claims.

title.en: Issue the privacy policy set to the workforce

description.en: Distribute the values, conditions and responsibility record to everyone bound by them, by whatever means the organisation uses to put a policy in front of staff, and record which version reached whom and when. This closes on the distribution record; instruction on what the responsibilities mean is delivered separately.

evidenceHint.en: Distribution record showing the policy version issued, the population it went to, and the date each part of that population received it.

title.en: Identify the privacy duties the current role map leaves unowned

description.en: A responsibility record is fixed against the role map of the day it was written, and then people leave, teams merge, posts are renamed and work is handed to a contractor, so a duty ends up recorded against a role nobody now holds — or split until two people each assume the other carries it. Work outward from the current staff and role list, naming the person accountable today for each recorded privacy responsibility, rather than reading the record and judging it plausible; a record that only looks coherent is exactly what decay produces. Catch the reverse case too, where staff are performing data actions from a role the record assigns no privacy responsibility at all, and settle each unowned duty on a named role instead of noting it.

evidenceHint.en: Per-responsibility check naming the role each duty is recorded against, who holds that role today, and every duty found with no accountable person together with where it was placed.

templates.title: Coordinating privacy roles internally and externally
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P4: Privacy roles and responsibilities are coordinated and aligned with third-party stakeholders (e.g., service providers, customers, partners).
templates.objective: To ensure privacy work spanning two functions or two organisations is divided so that every step has one side that performs it and none falls into the space between them.
templates.successCriteria:
Privacy activities crossing a function or organisational boundary are inventoried, with those under a deadline marked.
Each shared activity is split into steps allocated to a named holder on both sides.
Every part of a deadlined activity carries its own deadline, not only the activity as a whole.
A replayed case shows each step performed by one side, with handover gaps and duplications recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of cross-boundary privacy activities naming the internal functions and external parties holding a piece of each.
Obtain the split sheets allocating steps to each side, with the holder and deadline recorded per part.
Collect the reconstruction of each case replayed across the boundary, showing who carried out each step.
Request the correspondence exchanged with the other side for the cases replayed.

Analysis:
Read the split sheets for steps allocated to nobody and for steps each side believes the other performs.
Add the per-part deadlines for a deadlined activity and compare the total with the deadline the activity itself must meet.
Follow each reconstruction against its split sheet and mark where the sequence actually performed departed from the allocation.
Confirm the named holder on the external side is a role the other organisation recognises, not a personal contact.

Output:
Allocation matrix of cross-boundary steps against the holder on each side.
Deadline arithmetic setting per-part totals against the overall obligation.
Reconstruction findings listing each step nobody performed and each performed twice.

title.en: Map the privacy work that no single function or party completes alone

description.en: List the privacy activities that cannot be finished inside one function or one organisation, and for each name every holder of a piece — privacy, security, legal, a service provider, a customer, a partner. Start from the activities with a clock on them, because a seam only announces itself when a deadline runs across it. Skip this and the alignment work covers whichever seams somebody happened to remember, while the unclaimed ones stay invisible until a real case lands on them.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of cross-boundary privacy activities naming the internal functions and external parties holding a piece of each, with those under a deadline marked.

title.en: Divide each shared privacy duty into the part each side performs

description.en: For every privacy activity that crosses a boundary, write down which steps the organisation performs, which the other party performs, what passes between them and by when — a contract saying a provider will "assist" names no step and so leaves the work unallocated. Do the same for the internal seams: privacy, security and legal each hold a piece of a breach assessment or an individual's request, and the piece none of them claims is the one that stalls. Put a named holder on each side of every split, with the deadline that attaches to their part. This captures the working split between the parties; the clause that obliges a party belongs in the requirements register, and instructing that party on what it means is delivered under the awareness control.

evidenceHint.en: Split sheet listing every cross-boundary activity, the steps allocated to each organisation or function, the named holder on both sides, and the deadline against each part.

title.en: Replay a case that crossed the boundary and find the step neither side took

description.en: An agreed split holds on paper until something actually travels across the seam. Take cases from the period that ran through more than one function or party — a request answered out of a provider's store, an incident first seen on a partner's side, a deletion that had to propagate outward — and reconstruct who did each step and at what point they knew it was theirs. A step done twice is as much a defect as a step nobody did, because both show the two sides were working from different splits. Raise the correction against the split itself and the counterparts named in it, not against the individual case.

evidenceHint.en: Reconstruction of each case examined, showing the sequence of steps, who carried out each one, and every gap or duplication found at the handover.

templates.title: Legal, regulatory and contractual requirements
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P5: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding privacy are understood and managed.
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation can say which privacy obligations bind it and on what test, and keeps that answer current as instruments are amended and new agreements are signed.
templates.successCriteria:
The scope statement names the jurisdictions, sectoral regimes and classes of agreement swept, and the criterion deciding inclusion.
A disputed reading of whether an obligation applies is settled by the named authority and the outcome recorded.
The register carries each applicable requirement, its source, and the obligation it places on the organisation.
Each amendment, new instrument or renegotiated agreement in the period produces a register entry added, altered or withdrawn.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scope statement naming the jurisdictions, regimes and classes of agreement in the sweep and the inclusion criterion.
Obtain the register of legal, regulatory and contractual privacy requirements with the source cited for each entry.
Collect the dated review notes listing the changes picked up in the period and the register entry made for each.
Request the record of any disputed applicability question and the reading settled on.

Analysis:
Apply the inclusion criterion to the organisation's current markets, sectors and customer agreements and identify obligations the register omits.
Verify a sample of register entries against the instrument itself to confirm the obligation is recorded as the source states it.
Compare the period the review covered with the dates of known changes in the relevant regimes and identify changes never picked up.
Check that withdrawn entries were withdrawn against a source that actually ceased to apply rather than against an assumption.

Output:
Applicability worksheet applying the inclusion criterion to current operations.
Verification results for the sampled register entries against their sources.
List of changes in the period with the register action taken, and of changes found unrecorded.

title.en: Define the test that decides whether a privacy obligation binds the organisation

description.en: With no stated test, the register ends up being whatever the person compiling it already knew: the home statute goes in, a customer's processing addendum and a published certification commitment do not, and a duty that attaches because an individual lives somewhere else is never considered. Name the classes of source to be swept — statutes and regulations in each jurisdiction the organisation reaches, sector regimes, supervisory guidance, customer and supplier agreements, and commitments the organisation has made publicly — and the criterion that puts one inside the boundary or outside it. Name who rules on a contested reading as well, because two competent lawyers read the same clause differently and a register with no tie-breaker quietly carries both answers.

evidenceHint.en: Scope statement naming the jurisdictions, sectoral regimes and classes of agreement in the sweep, the criterion for inclusion, and the person who settles a disputed reading.

title.en: Compile the register of legal, regulatory and contractual privacy requirements that apply

description.en: List every legal, regulatory and contractual source that imposes a privacy requirement on the organisation, state in plain terms what each requires it to do, and name the internal policy or process that answers it. Where a requirement has nothing answering it, leave the row visible and name its owner.

title.en: Find the obligations that changed or arrived since the register was compiled

description.en: A requirement register decays from the outside in: the entries already written stay readable while a statute is amended, a regulator reissues its guidance, a customer contract is renegotiated at renewal, or the business opens in a market whose regime nobody has read. Work from the sources that know about change — horizon-scanning subscriptions, the contract renewal log, the period's new products and markets — because re-reading the register can only surface entries that are wrong, never obligations that were never entered. For each change decide whether it amends an entry, adds one, or retires one, and say which. This pass tests the statements of what is required, not whether the organisation is complying with them.

evidenceHint.en: Dated review note listing each amendment, new instrument, reissued guidance and renegotiated agreement picked up in the period, the source it came from, and the entry added, altered or withdrawn for it.

templates.title: Privacy risk in governance and risk management
templates.description: Implements GV.PO-P6: Governance and risk management policies, processes, and procedures address privacy risks.
templates.objective: To ensure privacy risk is carried by the organisation's own governance and risk machinery rather than handled as a separate exercise running alongside it.
templates.successCriteria:
Privacy risk appears in the enterprise risk register under its own category, with a named owner on every entry.
Harm to individuals is scored by a written rule rather than left to each scorer's sense of business impact.
Each governance instrument in scope either carries a privacy provision or has a change raised against it.
Instruments excluded from scope are recorded with the reason they were excluded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the signed scoping note listing the governance and risk instruments in scope, their owners and the exclusions.
Export the enterprise risk register filtered to the privacy category.
Obtain the written rule for scoring harm to individuals.
Collect the review note recording each governance or risk policy read for a privacy provision.
Retrieve the changes raised against instruments found silent on privacy.

Analysis:
Check that every register entry in the privacy category names an owner who is a current post-holder.
Re-score a sample of privacy entries using the written harm rule and compare the result with the score recorded.
Read each in-scope instrument against the review note and confirm the privacy provision cited is actually present in it.
Identify in-scope instruments that were reviewed but produced neither a provision nor a raised change.
Weigh the recorded exclusion reasons against the processing the organisation actually performs.

Output:
A schedule of privacy register entries showing category placement and owner status.
A re-scoring comparison for the sampled entries.
A list of governance instruments still silent on privacy, with the change raised against each.
Notes on exclusions accepted or challenged.

title.en: Settle which enterprise risk documents and forums privacy must be written into

description.en: "Our risk framework already covers privacy" stays unfalsifiable until somebody names the documents, and each owner can point at another owner's procedure. Name the instruments in scope — the enterprise risk policy, the risk taxonomy, the risk committee's terms of reference, the risk acceptance procedure, the internal audit plan — and for each state what would count as covering privacy risk, because a passing mention is not coverage. Note the instruments deliberately left outside and why, so the check that follows works from a fixed list rather than an impression of what was meant to be included.

evidenceHint.en: Signed scoping note listing each in-scope instrument, its owner, the bar it must meet for privacy, and the exclusions with reasons.

title.en: Give privacy risk its own category, owner and entry in the enterprise risk register

description.en: A privacy risk kept on a list the privacy function maintains for itself never competes for money or attention against the risks executives already watch, and one filed under "compliance" or "IT" loses the thing that defines it — the harm lands on people rather than on the balance sheet. Open a privacy category in the enterprise risk taxonomy, raise entries there for the privacy risks already known, and give each an accountable owner drawn from the same population that owns every other entry. The awkward part is scoring: enterprise impact scales are written as loss to the organisation, so set down how harm to individuals is expressed on that scale, or privacy entries will be rated low by default and drop below the line that gets treated.

evidenceHint.en: Register export showing each privacy entry under its new category with a named owner, plus the written rule for scoring harm to individuals.

title.en: Confirm the organisation's governance and risk policies address privacy risk

description.en: Read the governance and risk-management policies that are not privacy-specific and record, for each, where privacy risk is addressed and where it is silent. Raise the change needed for each silence and name who will make it.

evidenceHint.en: Review note naming each governance or risk policy read, the privacy provision found in it, and the changes raised where none was found.

templates.title: Agreed risk management processes
templates.description: Implements GV.RM-P1: Risk management processes are established, managed, and agreed to by organizational stakeholders.
templates.objective: To ensure privacy risks travel a route settled in advance, with a named forum holding authority to decide them and the functions bound by that route having agreed to it.
templates.successCriteria:
Every privacy risk raised can be shown to have reached the forum entitled to decide it.
The deciding body's terms of reference state its quorum and what becomes of a decision when quorum fails.
The functions bound by the process have recorded their agreement, and each objection lodged carries a resolution.
Escalation occurs at the point the agreed route specifies, not at the point someone chose to escalate.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the documented route for raising, deciding and escalating a privacy risk.
Collect the terms of reference for the deciding forum, including seats, the commitment each may make, quorum and current vacancies.
Gather the agreement record naming each stakeholder function, the date of agreement and any objection lodged.
Draw a sample of privacy risks raised during the period and pull the decision record that closed each one.

Analysis:
Trace each sampled risk from the date it was raised to the decision that closed it and compare the elapsed time with the agreed route.
Check that the person who settled each sampled risk held a seat carrying that authority on the date of the decision.
Test whether decisions were taken while a seat stood vacant or quorum was unmet, and whether the failure route was then followed.
Confirm every function bound by the process appears in the agreement record, and read the resolution recorded against each objection.

Output:
A trace of sampled privacy risks from raising to decision, with elapsed times.
An authority check comparing each decision-maker with the seat they held.
A list of stakeholder functions with agreement status and outstanding objections.
Findings where authority or timing departed from the agreed route.

title.en: Define how a privacy risk is raised, decided and escalated

description.en: Write down who may raise a privacy risk, who may decide a response at each level of severity, what must escalate and to whom, and what happens when a decision is not taken. Attach the process description; it is the thing stakeholders are later asked to agree to.

title.en: Name the forum that decides a privacy risk and the authority each seat carries

description.en: A process is only as agreed as the people who can be held to it, so name the body that takes privacy risk decisions, who sits on it, and what each seat can commit — accept on behalf of a business line, fund a treatment, overrule a product date. State the quorum and what happens when it is not met, because a decision taken by whoever attended is the failure this requirement is about: the process was established, and then not managed. Record where a seat is vacant rather than letting the remaining members absorb it silently.

evidenceHint.en: Terms of reference for the deciding body: seats, the commitment each may make, quorum, the escalation when quorum fails, and any seat currently vacant.

title.en: Obtain agreement to the process and tolerance from the functions bound by them

description.en: Put the process description and tolerance statement to each function that has to apply them, and record each one's agreement or objection together with how objections were settled. An unanswered objection recorded is more useful than a signature that hides it.

evidenceHint.en: Agreement record naming each stakeholder function, the date, and any objection raised with its resolution.

title.en: Trace a sample of raised privacy risks through to the decision that closed them

description.en: Draw items from across the period, deliberately including ones nobody pressed for, and follow each from the moment it entered the register to the decision recorded against it: who decided, under what authority, and how long it waited before anyone did. A process can look healthy in aggregate while the items that embarrass someone are precisely the ones that never reach a decision, so the sample has to be drawn by the reviewer rather than offered up by the people running the register. Treat an item still open past the interval the process allows as a finding in its own right, not as work in progress, and note any decision taken by someone the process does not authorise to take it.

evidenceHint.en: Worked sample listing each item followed, the elapsed time from raising to resolution, the person who settled it, and the deviations found where authority or timing departed from the agreed route.

templates.title: Expressing organisational risk tolerance
templates.description: Implements GV.RM-P2: Organizational risk tolerance is determined and clearly expressed.
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation states how much privacy risk it will carry in terms concrete enough that a ranked risk can be placed inside or outside the limit without argument.
templates.successCriteria:
The tolerance names the measure it caps and whether mitigations are counted before the comparison is made.
Harm to individuals and exposure to the organisation are held to limits that can be read separately.
A risk ranked during the period can be placed on one side of the threshold without further interpretation.
Decisions that accepted risk above the threshold carry a recorded escalation.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scoping note stating the measure the threshold applies to and whether mitigations are counted first.
Retrieve the expressed statement of privacy risk tolerance as currently approved.
Collect the privacy risks ranked during the period together with their scores.
Gather the review note comparing recent risk decisions against the stated tolerance.

Analysis:
Apply the tolerance to a sample of ranked risks and confirm each lands clearly on one side of the threshold.
Check whether the statement keeps the limit on harm to individuals distinguishable from the limit on organisational exposure.
Determine whether risks were compared before or after mitigation and whether that matches the scoping note.
Identify decisions that accepted risk above the threshold and follow each to its escalation record.

Output:
A placement table showing each sampled risk against the tolerance.
A note on whether the individual-harm and organisational-exposure limits are separable in practice.
A list of accepted risks above tolerance with their escalation status.
Any risk that could not be placed, with the ambiguity that prevented placement.

title.en: Settle what the privacy tolerance caps and whether it is read before or after controls

description.en: A tolerance means nothing until it is clear what it is applied to: the risk as it would stand with nothing mitigating it, or the risk left over once the controls the organisation actually runs are counted — the same sentence licenses very different processing under each reading. Decide that here, and decide whether the limit speaks to harm falling on individuals, exposure falling on the organisation, or two separate limits, because one figure covering both is always applied at its looser end. Write the decision down as the preamble the tolerance statement is then drafted against, so the level chosen later is not argued twice.

evidenceHint.en: Scoping note stating the measure the threshold applies to, whether mitigations are counted first, and whether harm to individuals and organisational exposure are held to separate limits.

title.en: Express the organisation's privacy risk tolerance in terms a ranked risk can be compared against

description.en: State what level of privacy risk the organisation will carry without further escalation and what it will not, using the same likelihood and impact terms in which risks are ranked, so a ranked risk can be placed against it without reinterpretation. A tolerance that cannot be compared to a ranking is a sentiment.

title.en: Compare recent risk decisions against the stated tolerance

description.en: Take the privacy risk decisions made since the last review and place each against the tolerance as written. Record every decision that fell outside it, whether it was escalated as the process requires, and what is being done about the ones that were not.

evidenceHint.en: Review note listing the decisions checked, the tolerance applied to each, and the decisions found outside tolerance with their escalation status.

templates.title: Tolerance informed by ecosystem role
templates.description: Implements GV.RM-P3: The organization's determination of risk tolerance is informed by its role in the data processing ecosystem.
templates.objective: To ensure it is the organisation's actual standing in the data processing ecosystem that moves its privacy threshold, and that the movement is reasoned on the record.
templates.successCriteria:
The facts admitted as inputs to the threshold are listed, each with the direction it is permitted to push.
The recorded justification names the roles the organisation actually holds rather than a generic position.
Roles taken on during the period are either reflected in the threshold or given a written disposition.
Inputs kept out of the reasoning carry the reason they were excluded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scoping note listing each ecosystem fact admitted as an input, the direction it may push and the exclusions.
Retrieve the written record of how the organisation's ecosystem role shaped the tolerance.
Collect the dated note naming each role held during the period and whether the reasoning addressed it.
Gather contracts, data flow records and service descriptions evidencing the roles actually held.

Analysis:
Compare the roles evidenced in contracts and data flows with the roles named in the recorded justification.
Check that each admitted input moved the threshold only in the direction it was permitted to push.
Identify roles held during the period that the justification never accounted for and read the disposition recorded for each.
Assess whether an excluded input would have altered the threshold had it been admitted.

Output:
A role comparison between evidenced practice and the recorded justification.
A list of admitted inputs with the direction each was allowed to move the threshold.
Unaccounted roles with the disposition recorded against them.
An assessment of exclusions that would have changed the threshold.

title.en: Decide which parts of the organisation's ecosystem standing may move the tolerance

description.en: Before any threshold is written, name the facts about where the organisation sits that its tolerance has to answer to: the roles it holds in each relationship, whose data it handles and at what volume, whether those individuals had any real choice, and who else builds on its output. Say which of those may push the tolerance down and which are not permitted to push it up, because a derivation written after the number is chosen will find a reason for whatever was already wanted. List the facts deliberately left out with the reason for each, so a later reader can tell an omission from a decision.

evidenceHint.en: Scoping note listing each fact admitted as an input to the threshold, the direction it is allowed to push, and the ones excluded with reasons.

title.en: Record how the organisation's ecosystem role shaped that tolerance

description.en: For each role the organisation holds in the data processing ecosystem, explain why the tolerance sits where it does — a party acting on another's behalf carries a different exposure than one deciding for itself, and a party others depend on carries more than one that stands alone. Attach the reasoning to the tolerance statement.

title.en: Find the ecosystem roles the tolerance's justification never accounted for

description.en: Take the relationships opened, altered or inherited since the tolerance was last justified — a first processing mandate for a regulated client, a service other firms now build their own products on, a sub-processor engaged on the organisation's own initiative — and check whether the reasoning attached to the tolerance names each one. A justification written while the organisation processed only for itself keeps reading plausibly after it has become a party others depend on, because nothing in it names the role that moved. For each role the reasoning misses, record whether the tolerance stands as written, shifts, or is held open until the body that owns it decides.

evidenceHint.en: Dated note naming each role the organisation held during the period, whether the tolerance reasoning addressed it, and what was decided about the ones it missed.

templates.title: Workforce privacy awareness and training
templates.description: Implements GV.AT-P1: The workforce is informed and trained on its roles and responsibilities.
templates.objective: To ensure every part of the workforce is told what privacy asks of it in its own work, and that delivery is tracked to the individual rather than reported in aggregate.
templates.successCriteria:
Each internal audience has a stated capability the instruction is meant to produce.
Completion records name the people reached and the version of the material they received.
Anyone on the audience list who was not reached has a follow-up recorded against them.
No part of the workforce sits outside every audience on the list.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the audience list with the capability defined for each audience.
Collect the completion record per audience showing names reached, material version and dates.
Retrieve the gap list of outstanding recipients with the follow-up taken against each.
Gather the workforce roster covering the period, including joiners and movers.

Analysis:
Reconcile the audience list against the workforce roster and identify people who belong to no audience.
Compare completion records with the roster to find recipients marked reached who had already left, and joiners never added to an audience.
Check that the material version delivered to each audience was the version current on the delivery date.
Follow each unreached person to the follow-up recorded and to the position they currently hold.

Output:
A reconciliation of audiences against the workforce roster.
A completion report per audience naming the version delivered.
A list of people covered by no audience or reached with superseded material.
Outstanding recipients with their follow-up and current position.

title.en: Identify the audiences needing privacy instruction and what each must be able to do

description.en: Separate the general workforce, senior executives, staff holding named privacy duties, and external parties, and for each record the responsibilities they must be able to carry out afterwards. Draw those responsibilities from the recorded role responsibilities and party obligations rather than restating generic privacy topics.

title.en: Deliver the instruction to each internal audience and record completion

description.en: Deliver to the workforce, the senior executives and the staff holding named privacy duties, by whatever means suits each, and record completion per person. Record separately, for the executive and privacy-duty audiences, what their session covered that the general one did not.

evidenceHint.en: Completion record per audience showing the names reached, the material version delivered, and the dates.

title.en: Check delivery against the audience list and follow up those not reached

description.en: Compare the completion and briefing records against the audience list, name every person and party still outstanding, and record the follow-up taken for each. Record anyone who cannot be reached and what is being done about their access instead.

evidenceHint.en: Gap list naming each outstanding recipient, the follow-up taken, and the position of anyone who remained unreached.

templates.title: Senior executives understand their roles
templates.description: Implements GV.AT-P2: Senior executives understand their roles and responsibilities.
templates.objective: To ensure directors and officers can recognise the privacy decisions reserved to them and answer for the ones they have taken, without the privacy team prompting them.
templates.successCriteria:
A board-adopted statement sets what a director or officer must recognise, decide and answer for on privacy.
Each senior executive has been walked through the approvals that cannot be signed below their level.
Executives answer questions on their privacy duties with no privacy specialist in the room.
Gaps exposed in questioning are carried into the next briefing rather than closed in the session.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the board-adopted statement of what is expected of a director or officer on privacy matters.
Collect the dated briefing pack and attendance note for the board and officer session.
Retrieve the list of approvals reserved to senior executives.
Gather the notes from each one-to-one questioning session, naming the post held and the questions put.

Analysis:
Check each sitting director and officer against the attendance note and identify those never briefed.
Compare the reserved approvals list with approvals actually signed in the period and find any signed below the reserved level.
Read the questioning notes to judge whether answers were given unaided and where they fell short.
Follow each gap recorded in questioning into the agenda of the briefing that followed.

Output:
A briefing position for every sitting director and officer.
A comparison of reserved approvals against the signatures obtained.
A summary of questioning outcomes by post held.
Gaps carried forward, with the briefing each was added to.

title.en: Set the standard of privacy understanding required of the board and the executive team

description.en: Write down what a director or officer is expected to recognise, decide and answer for, and how that differs from the day-to-day practice the workforce is taught. Without that line drawn, the board assumes privacy is discharged by whoever holds the specialist title, while the specialist assumes risks were accepted at a level that never actually saw them. Name the posts the standard binds — board members, committee chairs, officers, and the directors of any subsidiary carrying its own statutory exposure — because personal liability follows the seat rather than the reporting line.

evidenceHint.en: Board-adopted statement of what a director or officer is expected to recognise, decide and answer for on privacy matters.

title.en: Walk each senior executive through the privacy decisions reserved to them

description.en: Take the decisions that cannot be settled below board or officer level — accepting a privacy risk that sits outside the stated tolerance, funding or cutting privacy work, approving a launch or an acquisition that changes what the organisation processes, authorising notification after a breach — and show each executive what signing one commits the organisation to and what they personally answer for afterwards. An executive who only sits through the workforce session learns handling rules they will never apply themselves and none of the choices that arrive solely at their level. Leave operational procedure out of it: the work is recognising a privacy decision when it arrives dressed as a budget line, a launch date or a deal.

evidenceHint.en: Dated briefing pack and attendance note for the board and officer session, listing each approval that cannot be signed at a lower level.

title.en: Question each executive on their privacy duties without the privacy team present

description.en: Accountability at this level is personal: a regulator's interview, an investor question or a journalist's call goes to the chief executive, and the organisation finds out at that moment whether the understanding was real or borrowed from a slide deck. Sit with each named executive alone and ask what processing would hurt people most if it went wrong, which privacy decision is currently theirs to take, and what they would do in the first hour of a breach. Deferring the answer to the privacy team is the finding, not a pass. Carry each gap into the next briefing rather than filing it with the attendance record.

evidenceHint.en: Notes from each one-to-one session naming the post held, the questions put, and the gaps carried into the next briefing.

templates.title: Privacy personnel understand their roles
templates.description: Implements GV.AT-P3: Privacy personnel understand their roles and responsibilities.
templates.objective: To ensure the holders of privacy duties are equal to the judgements that terminate with them, and stay so as the legal and product sources beneath those judgements move.
templates.successCriteria:
Each named privacy duty has a syllabus drawn from the judgements that stop with its holder.
The sources whose movement would change a correct answer are tracked and named.
Holders and their stand-ins are re-tested on cases whose correct answer has since changed.
Answers given in re-testing are graded against a sourced position rather than the assessor's view.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the syllabus for each named privacy duty, with the judgements it terminates and the depth required of the holder.
Retrieve the list of legal and product sources tracked for change, with the dates of the changes recorded.
Collect the instruction material prepared for each audience of privacy specialists.
Gather the dated re-test records naming each holder and stand-in, the case put and the answer given.

Analysis:
Match each named privacy duty to a current holder and a stand-in, and identify duties left with neither.
Compare the recorded source changes with the cases used in re-testing to see whether moved answers were actually exercised.
Check that the position each answer was graded against cites its source, and re-derive that position for a sample.
Assess whether the instruction material reaches the depth the syllabus demands for the hardest judgements.

Output:
A duty-to-holder map including stand-ins and unfilled duties.
A schedule of source changes with the re-test case that exercised each.
A regrading of sampled answers against re-derived positions.
Coverage findings where material falls short of the syllabus depth.

title.en: Draw the privacy specialists' instruction from the decisions that stop with them

description.en: Everyone else's privacy instruction ends in "raise it with the privacy function", which has nobody to pass it to — so list the questions that terminate there and make those the syllabus: assessing a newly proposed processing activity, ruling on the ground it relies on, judging whether a data set is disassociated enough to leave, calling a notification inside its deadline. Against each, name the depth its holder needs and the outside sources whose movement makes yesterday's answer wrong, so currency has something specific to track rather than a yearly refresher. Scoped as awareness instead, the specialist ends up fluent in the policy and unable to apply it to the one case nobody else is positioned to decide.

evidenceHint.en: Syllabus per named privacy duty listing the judgements it terminates, the depth required of its holder, and the legal or product sources tracked for change.

title.en: Prepare the instruction material for each audience

description.en: Produce material addressed to each audience's own responsibilities — what they decide, what they must not do, and who they escalate to — rather than one set of slides shown to everyone. Attach the material per audience and name who approved its content.

title.en: Re-test the privacy specialists against decisions whose correct answer has since changed

description.en: A specialist's knowledge fails at the edges that moved — a regulator's changed position, a processing pattern the product did not have last year, an obligation it has newly fallen under — not at the material learned once. Take decisions the privacy function actually made in the period where the right answer would now differ, put them back to each duty holder and to whoever covers the duty while the holder is away, and settle the correct answer from the source text rather than from what the holder says it is. A specialist answering as they did a year ago is current in attendance only, and nothing downstream catches it: the workforce escalated precisely because it could not judge the question itself.

evidenceHint.en: Dated re-test record naming each holder and stand-in questioned, the case put to them, the answer given, and the source-based position it was measured against.

templates.title: Third parties understand their roles
templates.description: Implements GV.AT-P4: Third parties (e.g., service providers, customers, partners) understand their roles and responsibilities.
templates.objective: To ensure the privacy obligations a counterparty signed up to are understood by the staff who must actually perform them, and that the route to those staff works when used.
templates.successCriteria:
Each act required of a counterparty's people traces back to the contract term it derives from.
Briefings are recorded party by party, including the ones declined or left unanswered.
A privacy request sent to a party's ordinary front line reaches a handler without the account manager relaying it.
A response that misses the contracted window produces a re-brief of that party.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the per-engagement operating brief mapping each required act to its contract term and the function it was addressed to.
Collect the briefing record per party naming responsibilities covered, recipients and dates.
Retrieve the probe log showing the channel used, the date sent, who responded and the elapsed time.
Gather the contracts with their privacy clauses and stated response windows.

Analysis:
Trace a sample of required acts back to the contract term cited and confirm the term bears the meaning the brief gives it.
Compare the population of parties in the contract register with the parties actually briefed.
Measure each probe response against the contracted window and note where it was handled by the account manager rather than the front line.
Follow each failed probe to the re-brief raised and to whether that re-brief was delivered.

Output:
A traceability sample running from operating-brief acts to contract terms.
A briefing position per party, including declined and unanswered briefings.
Probe results with elapsed times measured against contracted windows.
Re-briefs raised, with their delivery status.

title.en: Translate each third party's privacy clauses into instructions its own staff can follow

description.en: The entity that signs a data processing agreement is never the person holding an individual's deletion request at nine on a Tuesday morning, and a clause drafted to allocate liability tells that person nothing about what to do next. For each engagement, work the binding terms down into the short set of acts the other side's people must actually perform — what to do when someone asks them for their data, what they may not collect on our behalf, whom to call and inside how many hours on a suspected breach — written in their queues, their vocabulary and their clock rather than ours. Address each set to the function that touches the data and name a holder there, because material that lands only with the account team or the signatory reaches nobody who will ever use it.

evidenceHint.en: Per-engagement operating brief showing, for each act required of the counterparty's people, the contract term it derives from and the function it was addressed to.

title.en: Brief each external party on the privacy responsibilities it holds

description.en: Take the obligations recorded for each ecosystem party and put them to the people at that party who must act on them, through the channel that relationship uses. Record which party was briefed, what was covered and who received it, including parties that declined.

evidenceHint.en: Per-party briefing record naming the party, the responsibilities covered, the recipients and the date, including declined or unanswered briefings.

title.en: Route a test privacy request to each external party's front line, not its account manager

description.en: A signed agreement plus a relationship manager who says yes, our people know is not evidence that anyone on the floor recognises the request when it lands. Put a real-shaped one — an individual asking for their data, or a suspected-breach report — into the same inbox, portal or number a customer or subcontractor would actually reach, then follow it: who picked it up, whether they recognised what it was, and whether it came back inside the window the contract sets. This is the only lever available here, since the organisation cannot order a supplier's staff onto a course and cannot see its induction records; what it can do is observe behaviour and re-brief the function that dropped the request. Tell the party afterwards that the probe was a test, so the co-operation the next one depends on survives it.

evidenceHint.en: Probe log per party: channel used, date sent, who responded, elapsed time against the contracted window, and the re-brief raised where it went wrong.

templates.title: Ongoing re-evaluation of privacy risk
templates.description: Implements GV.MT-P1: Privacy risk is re-evaluated on an ongoing basis and as key factors, including the organization's business environment and data processing, change.
templates.objective: To ensure a privacy risk assessment is reopened when the conditions it rested on move, and that an assessment left standing is aged by decision rather than by neglect.
templates.successCriteria:
The changes that force a reassessment are defined in advance rather than judged after the event.
Every signed-off assessment carries a dated snapshot of the factor values it was made against.
A triggered change produces a re-evaluation record naming the trigger and what moved in the risk or its response.
Assessments past their interval have a disposition recorded, whether redone or deliberately left standing.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the definition of the changes that force privacy risk to be re-evaluated.
Collect the dated factor snapshots filed against signed-off assessments, with the source each value was read from.
Retrieve the re-evaluation records produced during the period, with the trigger and the outcome of each.
Gather the ordered list of standing assessments with their last-revisited dates and dispositions.

Analysis:
Compare current factor values with the snapshot filed against each assessment and identify movements that should have forced a reassessment.
Check that each defined trigger which fired during the period produced a re-evaluation record.
Read the outcome of sampled re-evaluations to confirm the risk or its response was changed, or the lack of change was reasoned.
Test the ageing list against the interval applied and find assessments past that interval with no disposition.

Output:
A movement comparison between filed snapshots and current factor values.
A reconciliation of triggers fired against re-evaluation records produced.
Outcomes of the sampled re-evaluations.
An ageing schedule of standing assessments with missing dispositions flagged.

title.en: Define the changes that force privacy risk to be re-evaluated

description.en: List the events that require the risk assessment to be revisited — new or changed processing, a change of environment or party, a shift in the business, a problematic data action — and state who must be told when one occurs and within what the organisation itself sets. Attach the trigger list; it is what the later re-evaluations are measured against.

title.en: Take the current reading of every factor whose movement re-opens a risk assessment

description.en: A trigger list is unusable until every factor it names has a recorded value to compare against: nobody can say the processing volume, the jurisdictions, the vendor set or the population served has moved if the old state exists only in memory. Fix each factor's value on the day an assessment is signed off, store it with that assessment rather than in a register that ages on its own, and make it specific enough to compare mechanically, since a handful of EU customers cannot be tested against next year's figure. Include the factors that sit outside the organisation, such as the legal regime and the ecosystem position being relied on, because those move without anyone raising a change request.

evidenceHint.en: Dated snapshot filed against each signed-off assessment, giving the value of every watched factor at that moment and the source it was read from.

title.en: Re-evaluate privacy risk for each triggered change and record the outcome

description.en: When a listed trigger fires, revisit the affected part of the assessment and record what was reassessed, what changed in the ranking or responses, and what did not. Where a trigger fired and no re-evaluation followed, record that too, with the reason.

evidenceHint.en: Dated re-evaluation record naming the trigger, the processing reassessed, and the change made to the risk or its response.

title.en: Age the untouched privacy risk assessments and decide which must be redone

description.en: Trigger-driven re-evaluation has a blind spot where it looks safest: processing that nothing has happened to is never re-examined, while the ground under it shifts, as a regulator's interpretation hardens, the population grows, or a control quietly stops working. Order the standing assessments by the date each was last revisited, not by whoever has been asking about them, and send the oldest back through assessment on age alone with no trigger required. An assessment that has outlived the interval the organisation set for itself is a finding in its own right, not a scheduling problem to absorb.

evidenceHint.en: Ordered list of every standing assessment with its last-revisited date, the interval it was measured against, and the disposition recorded for each one past that interval.

templates.title: Reviewing values, policies and training
templates.description: Implements GV.MT-P2: Privacy values, policies, and training are reviewed and any updates are communicated.
templates.objective: To ensure a revision to privacy values, policy or instruction reaches every copy in circulation and every person already taught from the version it replaces.
templates.successCriteria:
Every derived copy of privacy material is registered with an owner, a current version and its place of publication.
A revision produces a replacement of each training module it touches rather than an addendum to the old one.
People who completed a superseded version are re-taught and recorded as having been re-taught.
Each revision records the trigger behind it and the way the change was communicated.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of privacy documents, modules and derived copies with owner, current version and publication location.
Collect the superseded and replacement versions of each module or deck revised during the period.
Retrieve the rosters of people re-taught, alongside the completion records for the earlier versions.
Gather the change record showing each revision, the trigger or incident behind it and the communication issued.

Analysis:
Visit the published locations named in the register and compare the version found there with the version recorded.
Compare each revision in the change record with the material actually reworked and find revisions that touched no module.
Reconcile the re-taught roster against those who had completed the superseded version and identify people left on the old content.
Check that the communication issued for each revision reached the audience the material is addressed to.

Output:
A published-version comparison for each registered location.
A revision-to-module mapping showing revisions that reworked nothing.
A re-teaching reconciliation naming people still holding superseded material.
A communication record per revision with the audience it reached.

title.en: Assemble the privacy material under review and every restatement of it in circulation

description.en: Gather the values statement, the privacy policies and standards, and the instruction material, then go one step further and find where those same rules are restated in someone else's words — a handbook section, an onboarding deck, an intranet answer, a contract annex, an induction quiz. Name the owner and the version of each, because a revision has to reach the restatements as well, and nobody maintains a copy they have not been told they hold. A review drawn up from the documents with privacy in the title leaves staff being taught last year's rule by material nobody counted.

evidenceHint.en: Register of the documents, modules and derived copies in scope, each with its owner, current version and the place it is published.

title.en: Rework the training material each privacy revision touches and reissue it to those already taught

description.en: When a rule is revised, the master document moves and everything downstream keeps teaching the old one — the induction deck, the quiz answers, the handbook paragraph, the slide a manager reuses. Work through the material tied to the revised rule, change what the revision actually changed, and mark the version now in force so a reader can tell which one they hold. Then put the change in front of the people who completed the earlier version: material updated only for new joiners leaves the population already taught confidently wrong.

evidenceHint.en: The superseded and replacement versions of each module or deck, with the date of issue and the roster of people re-taught against those who had completed the earlier version.

title.en: Review the privacy values, policies and instruction material and communicate what changed

description.en: Read them against what the organisation now does and against the problematic data actions handled since the last review, revise what no longer holds, and record what each change was for. Communicate the revisions to the people bound by them and record how.

evidenceHint.en: Change record showing each revision made, the trigger or incident behind it, and how the change was communicated.

templates.title: Assessing compliance with requirements
templates.description: Implements GV.MT-P3: Policies, processes, and procedures for assessing compliance with legal requirements and privacy policies are established and in place.
templates.objective: To ensure legal requirements and the organisation's own privacy policies are tested against practice on stated pass conditions, so that a claim of compliance rests on evidence.
templates.successCriteria:
Every requirement and policy clause has a check naming the artefact to inspect, the population to sample and the result that counts as met.
Results are recorded clause by clause and every gap carries an owner.
A clause reported as met can be re-performed from the evidence retained for it.
Register rows the assessment never touched are counted rather than passed over in silence.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the assessment criteria sheet giving the artefact, population and pass condition for each requirement and policy clause.
Retrieve the requirements register and the privacy policies currently in force.
Collect the compliance assessment results with the owner recorded against each gap.
Gather the re-performance note naming the rows re-tested and the evidence examined for each.

Analysis:
Count the register rows and policy clauses against the rows the assessment actually reported on, and state the difference.
Re-perform a sample of clauses reported as met using the retained evidence and compare the verdict reached with the one recorded.
Check that each pass condition can be decided from the artefact named rather than requiring an unstated judgement.
Follow open gaps through to their owner and the remediation recorded against them.

Output:
A coverage figure of clauses assessed against clauses held in the register.
Re-performance results, naming any verdict that changed on re-test.
A list of pass conditions that could not be decided from the artefact named.
Open gaps with owners and remediation status.

title.en: Translate each requirement and policy clause into a check with a pass condition

description.en: The register states each obligation in the language of the law or the contract, which is not yet something anyone can test.
